title: PostgreSQL LISTEN and NOTIFY: Pub/Sub Architecture and Queue Hazards
realWorldScenario: An engineering team implements an event-driven microservice using PostgreSQL `LISTEN` and `NOTIFY` triggers on the `orders` table to notify a webhook service. During Black Friday, the database logs warnings about the notification queue filling up.
questionStatement: Explain how `LISTEN` and `NOTIFY` work internally in PostgreSQL. Where is the notification queue stored, what are the payload size limitations, and what occurs when the queue overflows? When should you use LISTEN/NOTIFY vs an external message broker like Kafka or RabbitMQ?
expectedConcepts: Transactional guarantees (NOTIFY is sent only upon commit)
Shared memory SLRU queue and queue overflow aborting transactions
Ephemeral nature (no message durability for offline listeners)
Appropriate use cases vs external message queues
hints: Does NOTIFY deliver messages if the enclosing transaction rolls back?
What happens if an unconsumed listener hangs for 4 hours while millions of notifications are fired?
